records.reading_scope: Complete substantive review read. Stoffman describes childhood/psychology/consumer culture and the 1960s argument, while challenging radical representativeness and aspects of the cohort explanation. Monograph unread.

records.source_title: Franca Iacovetta, University of Toronto Culinaria profile
records.reading_scope: Research identity, 2006 Gatekeepers and editorial publications checked. Page retains a 2014 conference announcement; not recent living evidence.

records.source_title: Tanya Basok and Marshall Bastable, “Knock, Knock, Knockin’ on Heaven’s Door”, Labour/Le Travail 63 (2009), 207–219
records.reading_scope: Complete review essay read; Iacovetta discussion especially 209–214. Reviewers analyze surveillance, liberal citizenship, gender/family and immigrant accommodation/resistance, and question the scope of exclusion. Other books in this joint review are not attributed to Iacovetta.

records.source_title: York University Elia Chair: Italian-Canadian studies bibliography
records.reading_scope: 1992 Such Hardworking People and 2000 Enemies Within checked; Enemies Within is co-edited with Roberto Perin and Angelo Principe, not solely authored.

records.source_title: Frederick Cooper, Human Centered interview and linked bibliography, CASBS
records.reading_scope: Transcript read, especially genealogy, concepts, sequences and imperial citizenship sections; audio not used. Episode notes date 1996, 2005 and 2010 books. Empires in World History is coauthored with Jane Burbank. This is an account of his research, not a reading of the monographs.
